items.title: Google's March 2026 Core Update Targets Thin AI Content
items.summary: Google rolled out a major core update in March 2026, emphasizing quality content over thin AI-generated material. Sites producing low-value AI content risk penalties, pushing SEO pros to focus on helpful, original resources. This update aligns with ongoing efforts to combat spam and misinformation.<grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">25</argument></grok:render>

items.title: SEO Test Reveals Ease of Ranking Misinformation on Google
items.summary: An experiment demonstrates how simple it is to manipulate Google rankings with misinformation via basic SEO tactics. This highlights vulnerabilities in current algorithms amid rising AI search changes. Experts urge stronger E-E-A-T signals and fact-checking in content strategies.<grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">7</argument></grok:render>

items.title: John Mueller Urges Focus on AI Search Beyond Traditional SEO
items.summary: Google's John Mueller advises businesses to consider AI search visibility alongside SEO, as ranking alone doesn't ensure appearances in tools like ChatGPT or Gemini. He emphasizes understanding site value in an AI world for sustained traffic. This signals a shift toward GEO and AEO strategies.<grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">55</argument></grok:render>

items.title: 90-Day Plan to Hit $10K/Mo from Scratch with SEO
items.summary: SEO expert Charles Floate shares a detailed 90-day blueprint to rebuild to $10k monthly revenue using only a laptop and minimal funds. It covers niche selection, AI-assisted content, authority building, and monetization in high-CPC areas. The plan leverages modern tools for rapid scaling.<grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">56</argument></grok:render>

items.title: New Claude Skill Optimizes Content for AI Search Citations
items.summary: Corey Haines launches /ai-seo, a Claude Code skill that audits pages for AI citation potential in tools like Perplexity and Google AI Overviews. It identifies fixes for structured data, direct answers, and entity signals to boost generative visibility. This tool represents the evolution to AEO/GEO optimization.<grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">63</argument></grok:render>

items.title: BookTok Trends Shift Towards Explicit Romance Content
items.summary: A discussion on X reveals BookTok's preference for romance novels often likened to porn, with explicit examples from Hoover and Gravia. Users contrast this with less explicit literary works like The Atlas Six and Secret History. The trend influences publishing channels focused on such content.

items.title: Criticism Mounts Over Shallow Tropes in Mainstream BookTok Romance
items.summary: X users criticize popular BookTok romance books for relying on clichés that appeal mainly to white, affluent audiences, lacking depth on race, class, or power dynamics. They argue these trends prioritize tropes over societal critique or complexity. Mainstream appeal drives the publishing focus on such stories.

items.title: Sci-Fi Author Questions Value of Hybrid Publishing Contract
items.summary: An author announces receiving a hybrid publishing contract offer and seeks community input on whether it's superior to self-publishing in profitability. Highlights ongoing debates in traditional vs. alternative publishing paths. Responses discuss upfront costs and promotion challenges.

items.title: Publishers Urged to Tackle AI Misinformation Before Reader Manipulation
items.summary: The Bookseller calls on publishers to address AI-generated misinformation immediately to protect readers. References BookTok phenomena like Sarah J. Maas causing meltdowns. Emphasizes proactive measures in the evolving publishing landscape.

items.title: Literary Agents Warn Writers Against Using AI in Submissions
items.summary: Agents observe a 'change in the nature of submissions' due to AI and urge writers to avoid it. Highlights concerns over quality and authenticity in writing. Ties into broader AI controversies impacting editing and publishing.

items.title: Recent Book Deals Announced for March 2026
items.summary: Publishers Weekly details major contracts including a two-book deal at Random House for Chantal V., acquired by Caitlin McKenna at auction. October release planned for one title. Showcases active deal-making in publishing.

items.title: Netflix's Woke Policies Blamed for Failed Warner Bros. Merger
items.summary: A viral post claims Netflix lost the Warner Bros. acquisition due to extreme woke policies like tampons in men's rooms, similar to Bud Light and Target. It portrays this as a victory for America against leftist ideologies embraced by Netflix executives. The post links to a NY Post article detailing the cultural clashes.

items.title: Actress Mocking Fans and Original Film Sparks Backlash
items.summary: High-engagement post criticizes an actress for mocking the original film, picking fights with fans, and refusing to take responsibility for backlash. She calls the reaction confusing and vows not to assimilate. The post warns studios against hiring her due to repeated poor judgments.

items.title: Company Announces Pride in No Employees Watching Oscars
items.summary: Satirical post from a golf account states the company is proud no employees watched the Oscars last night. It garners thousands of likes amid reports of declining viewership. Reflects audience disinterest in the award show.

items.title: Oscars 2026: Has Hollywood’s “Wokeism” Run Its Course?
items.summary: Article discusses growing audience backlash to celebrity activism and preachy messaging at Oscars 2026, with declining viewership numbers. Social media users decry Hollywood as out-of-touch activists prioritizing ideology over entertainment. Suggests shift to escapist content as studios face flops.

items.title: Woke Films Keep Flopping — and Hollywood Is Finally Listening
items.summary: Recent woke films experience box office bombs, prompting Hollywood recalibration. Pixar removes LGBT storyline from Elio after parent concerns about family content. Emphasis on profitability over ideology as audience rejects preachy narratives.

items.title: Paul Thomas Anderson Addresses Racial Criticism for Oscar-Winning Film
items.summary: Paul Thomas Anderson responds to backlash over portrayal of Black women in 'One Battle After Another' during Oscars acceptance speeches for Best Picture, Director, and Adapted Screenplay. The controversy surrounded the film since its release. He addressed criticisms amid the wins.

items.title: NEW SBE Council Tech Use Survey Reveals Rapid AI Adoption Among Small Businesses
items.summary: A new survey indicates that 82% of small businesses are using at least one AI tool, with 66% reporting revenue increases and median time savings of 5 hours per week for owners and 11.5 hours for employees. AI is seen as augmenting workers, with 40% of users planning to increase hiring and high optimism about competitiveness. Automated pricing tools are increasingly adopted, with 97% noting revenue gains.

items.title: AI Tools Boost Small Business Marketing and Content Efficiency
items.summary: More than 75% of small business owners use AI like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini for marketing, content production, and customer service, with over 90% finding them effective for productivity. Barriers like technical expertise and data privacy limit full integration, with only 14% embedding AI in core operations. These tools excel in copywriting and social media but are underused for revenue-generating tasks.

items.title: Google's Free AI Marketing Suite Transforms Small Business Promotion
items.summary: Google has released a free AI tool that scans a small business website to create tailored ads, social posts, headlines, CTAs, and animated video creatives matched to the brand. Unlike generic templates, it delivers customized marketing content available in over 170 countries. This update is hailed as one of the most significant free AI business tools for entrepreneurs.

items.title: AI Stacks Empower Solopreneurs and Small Businesses to Scale Efficiently
items.summary: Solopreneurs can replicate 5-person teams using affordable AI stacks: chatbots like Tidio for support, Claude/Jasper for content/marketing, and Zapier/Notion for operations. Total cost under $100/month yields 10-15 hours weekly savings, enabling competition with larger firms. Practical adoption focuses on customer service, admin, and growth tasks.
